body.statement: For fixed \(C\in\mathcal D_G\) and \(D\in\mathcal D_H\), every observable mixture law generated from \(C\) by arbitrary mutually independent nonconstant non-Gaussian real sources, with no location or moment restriction, is generated from \(D\) if and only if there exist a surjection \(f:U_C\twoheadrightarrow U_D\) and nonzero scalars \(a_i\) with \(C_{:,i}=a_iD_{:,f(i)}\) for every \(i\in U_C\).  Necessity is witnessed by admissible finite-support Bernoulli sources in their original jump lattice; sufficiency merges independent sources and preserves both nonconstancy and non-Gaussianity.
body.proof_tex:
For a matrix \(A\), the observable laws obtained by varying the unrestricted admissible source coordinates are exactly \(\mathscr L_{\mathrm{ng}}(A)\) in \(\text{lem:finite-mixture-containment-unrestricted}\).  Apply that lemma first with \(A=C\) and then with the candidate matrix \(D\).  It gives
\[
 \mathscr L_{\mathrm{ng}}(C)\subseteq\mathscr L_{\mathrm{ng}}(D)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists f:U_C\twoheadrightarrow U_D\ \exists(a_i)_{i\in U_C}\in
 (\mathbb R\setminus\{0\})^{U_C}\ \forall i\in U_C:
 C_{:,i}=a_iD_{:,f(i)}.
\]
The diagnostic lemma proves the claimed original-lattice necessity, including proportional source columns and invisible columns.  The constructive direction of the finite-mixture theorem gives the merged target sources.  Its independent-sum and L\'evy--Cram\'er arguments establish nonconstancy and non-Gaussianity without a variance or centering premise.  This is precisely the claimed equivalence.
body.justification: A finite Bernoulli diagnostic and original-lattice Laurent factorization eliminate arbitrary independent non-Gaussian source laws without centering or moments.
body.gap: Observational equivalence results do not expose this directed visible-source surjection theorem with invisible columns and irreversible source merging.
body.consumer: Both exact-support and zero-allowed compilers enumerate finite source-partition types instead of quantifying over probability laws.
